name: Wedding & event planner

pf.license.need: No state license for planning or coordinating weddings and events in most places. A local business license where the city or county asks for one: from the state form.
pf.license.travel: A planner who sells or books guests' travel or lodging may need a seller-of-travel registration where the state's rules require it: a switch from the state form. The example sells no travel.
pf.license.alcohol: A planner never serves or sells alcohol. The venue or a licensed bar does, under its own license.
pf.license.who holds it: The business holds any business license or registration. Planners need no license of their own.
what to ask: The business license or registration number, where the place asks for one
A seller-of-travel registration number, only if the business books guests' travel and the state's form asks
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: Nothing, unless the state's form makes a registration a must for a service the business offers. Then only that service waits.
pf.license.renewals: A reminder 30 days before a registration or the insurance runs out.
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance on file, with its end date. Many venues ask for a certificate that names them.
pf.license.background checks: Only where the state's form or a venue asks, like for an event at a school.

pf.services.capacity: One wedding a date for each lead planner, with an associate planner on the day. Meetings book the planner's own time.
pf.services.what Rosie never books: Other vendors. The couple signs and pays each vendor (venue, caterer, photographer, florist, DJ) directly. Rosie books and takes money only for the planner's own time and work.
pf.services.nobody needs to be home: Never: a planner works with the couple or at the event.
pf.services.online: The free first call, planning meetings and consults can be video calls. Consults are held only at the studio or by video.

pf.visit.check-in at the studio: The code at the desk, or read out at the start of a video meeting.
pf.visit.check-in at the venue: The code, given to the lead planner on arrival by the couple or a person named on the booking.
pf.visit.work changes at the event: An extra hour only with the couple's written yes by text, at the rate shown before booking. No yes in 10 minutes: the planners leave at the time booked.
pf.visit.vendors: The planner checks each vendor in against the timeline with their own tools. Rosie never texts, books or pays a vendor.
pf.visit.weather: Outdoor plans name a rain spot and a large enclosed building. The planner and the couple make the rain call by a set time on the day.
pf.visit.proof it's done: The lead planner texts DONE at the end of the meeting, or after the send-off and the wrap-up on the day.
pf.visit.results later: None: the planner's notes and timeline stay on the secure page and in the planner's own tools.

starting answers: Full and partial planning: a signed contract, a 30% retainer when booking, and the rest billed in stages, each when the planner texts DONE for it (the example: two stages of 35%); Rosie never bills on a date by itself
Month-of coordination: a signed contract, a 25% retainer, and the rest charged to the saved card when the day is done
Consults, at the studio or by video: paid in full when booking. An extra planning meeting: billed by text after. The free first call: nothing taken
An extra hour on the day: priced first, only with a written yes, paid with the rest
limits: Deposit or retainer cap: from the state form
Free to cancel for a set time after signing (the example: until 24 hours before the first planning meeting, or 3 days after signing for month-of)
After that, a cancel keeps only what the contract's dated schedule says, credited toward the work done, and the owner confirms it. No answer, nothing kept
A late payment gets one pay link and a note to the owner. Rosie never cancels a wedding over a late payment; the owner decides
The business cancels, or the couple says no to a stand-in planner: everything paid is refunded
pf.money.vendors: Rosie never takes, holds or passes on money for other vendors. Only the planner's own fee goes through, into the planner's own Stripe.
pf.money.extras: An extra planning meeting or an extra hour is billed only with the couple's yes.
pf.money.travel: Free within 40 miles; the example's $1 a mile round trip beyond.
pf.money.tips: Off. The couple's tips for vendors are handed out by the planner, in envelopes the couple gives; they never go through Rosie.
pf.money.tax: No tax line unless the owner sets a rate where the state taxes the service.
pf.money.Rosfield's $2: Applies: the business pays $2 per confirmed booking.

pf.messages.never in a text: The budget, the guest list, family details, access or health needs and gate codes stay on the secure page. Texts to the owner, the planners or the couple carry none of them: only names, dates, times, places and the planner's fee.
pf.messages.minors: A child in the wedding party (a flower girl or ring bearer) stays with a parent or a named adult. A planner never looks after a child alone.

pf.staff.supervision: None by state rule. An associate planner works with a lead on the day.
pf.staff.who OKs what: The owner OKs every planning quote, every amount kept on a cancel and any stand-in lead. The office manager may OK meeting changes if the owner sets it.
pf.staff.stand-ins: A lead planner the owner trusts, even from outside the team, only if the couple agrees. On no reply, nobody is swapped in: the owner calls the couple.

pf.rules.written contract: The business's own contract, filled in from the booking, signed by each partner named and the business before money is taken, for every planning or coordination booking. Any parts the state's rules add come from the state form.
pf.rules.date hold: The date stays saved for 2 days while the contract is signed (the owner's setting), with a next-in-line list.
pf.rules.one a date: One wedding a date per lead planner, booked up to 24 months ahead (the owner's settings).
pf.rules.cancel schedule: Free to cancel for a set time after signing. After that, a dated schedule from the contract, never the whole fee. One free date move 6 months or more ahead, if a planner is free (the owner's setting).
pf.rules.meetings: Each planning meeting is its own booking under the contract. A meeting missed without 24 hours' notice counts as used only with the owner's OK.
pf.rules.vendors: Each vendor contract is between the couple and the vendor. The planner may suggest vendors, but never takes a payment from a vendor through Rosie.
pf.rules.venue rules: Load-in times, the end time, noise limits and insurance certificates come from the venue: switches the planner sets for each venue.
pf.rules.records: Contracts and payments kept 7 years, as for every kind of work.
pf.rules.weather limit: A small outdoor party is checked against the forecast the day before (the owner's setting: heavy rain). A wedding has a rain plan instead, called on the day.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for planners:
planning and events: A late payment: one pay link and the owner decides; Rosie never cancels a wedding over it
The couple cancels: only what the dated schedule says is kept, with the owner's OK
The couple moves the date: one free move 6 months or more ahead, if a planner is free
The lead planner can't come on the day: a trusted stand-in if the couple agrees, or a full refund
A planning meeting missed without notice: counts as used only with the owner's OK
Rain or lightning at an outdoor event: the rain spot, and guests indoors until 30 minutes after the last thunder
A vendor runs late or doesn't come: the planner handles it on the day; Rosie never contacts the vendor
Asked to stay longer: an extra hour only with a written yes
A parent pays: the bill goes to them by a link the couple forwards
The couple opts out of texts: the booking stays, and the planner calls or emails

notes:
Refit Tue Oct 27 2026 (R14) to the REDESIGN 2 master: plug-in facts (photos: quoted after a free first call, documents: the planning contract, video: meetings by video, stages: the rest billed in stages, each when the planner texts DONE for it, A9-16), no switches, settings (set start; free cancel until 24 hours before), money facts per path with names, rename pairs, few ops. The master never bills or charges on a set date by itself (D66 #7): full planning's two set payments are now stages billed at DONE (A9-16), and month-of's rest is charged to the saved card at DONE after the day. A's free first call is now its own free path (list|none|none). Flow B's wedding now follows the master's calendar (Thu Oct 22 at Cedar Hill Farm; rehearsal Wed Oct 21). Every old say/vary words op is gone (the record words retainers, fees and refunds now). Kept: valid off ops, own branches (the rehearsal, the rain call, a late vendor; 'his own tools' -> the planners').
Pilot: from photographer. Wedding planning runs like event photography on the day: a date held while a contract is signed, a retainer, the rest before the event, venue rules and an insurance certificate, an extra hour agreed on the night, and a stand-in for a date that can't move. The coach's free intro call (a first call with a named professional) was the model for the free first call; caterer, DJ and makeup were read for event words. The renames were rebuilt from the master: the planner's paths differ from the photographer's (flow A's main path is quoted, not from a list).
Cast: Sam Lee's main company is Lee Weddings & Events LLC (410 Market St; the master's Lee Home Services): event coordination, with corporate events as its second kind of work (trade names Lee Weddings and Lee Corporate Events). His second company is Lee Planning Studio LLC (64 Rose St; the master's barbershop): wedding planning at the studio or by video. Planners Nadia (lead, full planning) and Elena (associate) are the studio's (Riley, Avery); Julian (lead planner, also leads corporate events) and Gabe (associate) run event days (Jordan, Casey). Carmen Ruiz is a lead planner Sam trusts from outside the team. Alex M.'s partner is Robin (the master's Jamie). Sam and Pat are kept.
Flow A, the usual side for the booking itself: Alex and Robin (wedding Sat Jun 12, 2027) ask for a planner who can run everything. A4-07 sets up a free 45-minute first call with Nadia (Thu Oct 22, 12:00pm, at the studio or by video); Nadia quotes full planning at $8,500 after it (A4-08), Sam OKs every planning quote (A4-09), both partners and Sam sign the contract on the secure page (A5-20), a $2,550 retainer (30%) holds the date (A5-13). The visit in flow A is the first planning meeting at the studio, Sat Oct 24, 11:00am (code 5160). The rest comes in two set payments of $2,975, each billed by text a week before its date: Sat Dec 12, 2026 (six months before) and Thu May 13, 2027 (30 days before) (A9-05, A9-16). The rating comes once, after the wedding (A10-02).
Flow B, the other side: Alex and Robin planned their own wedding at Cedar Hill Farm (14 Orchard Rd) and book month-of coordination. Julian holds a free first call (Tue Oct 20, 12:00pm by video), quotes $2,400 (B4-09), Sam OKs it, all three sign (B4-61, B4-58), a $600 retainer (25%) holds Sat May 22, 2027 (B5-11), the final walkthrough at the farm is booked as the first step (B4-40; result B7-37), the $1,800 rest is charged on the set day, Thu Apr 22, 2027 (B7-24), the rehearsal is the day before (own branch B7-x01), and Julian and Gabe run the day from 12:00pm (B8). An extra hour on the night ($150 a planner, $300) is asked by text and paid by one pay link the next morning (B8-23, B9-04).
Money paths. A: photos|deposit|bill (main: full planning quoted after the free first call, retainer, set payments billed by text), list|full|none (a $150 planning consult, paid in full, for couples planning it themselves), list|none|bill (an extra $150 planning meeting after a contract's included meetings are used, billed after). B: photos|deposit|none (month-of coordination: retainer, the rest charged on the set day, day-of overtime by one pay link). The price kind 'quoted from photos first' reads 'Quoted after a free first call' (labels). Left out: holds, the saved card charged at DONE, the business's own way, a counter, and A's photos|deposit|none (a set day before the first meeting isn't how planners take installments). B's on-site consult (list|full|none) was dropped: it's the same money way as A's consult, and its October dates can't share flow B's months-long what-ifs.
The free first call is the quote step (A4-07 to A4-12, B4-08 to B4-13), not a first step: no date is saved while it's quoted, and the quote is good for 5 days. A4-43 keeps 'No', 'Already on file' (a call in the last 3 months) and the planning questionnaire on the secure page (A4-72, B4-86).
Installments: the master has one set day. Flow A bills the two payments by text (after:bill), the second as A9-05's bill and the last as A9-16 (paid in stages); flow B charges one rest on the set day. Gap 'Several set payments before an event'.
Included meetings: each planning meeting is booked on its own under the contract (A10-07). A missed meeting keeps no money: A8-14 to A8-22, A8-46 to A8-64 and S11-23 to S11-28 ask Sam to count it as one of the 10 (no answer: not counted). Gap 'Meetings included in a contract, counted down'.
Cancels: A free until 24 hours before the first meeting (Fri Oct 23, 11am); B free for 3 days after signing (until Fri Oct 23, 7pm, reminded by B7-01). After that, the contract's dated schedule, never the whole fee and always with Sam's OK: A keeps up to $1,500 before Dec 12, $4,250 before May 13, then $6,800; B keeps the $600 retainer, and from Apr 22 up to $1,800. These amounts are the example's own and become a state-form switch ('the state's rules on amounts kept').
Vendors: Rosie books and takes money only for the planner's own time and work. It never books, pays, texts or tracks other vendors (A4-38, B4-03, B7-x01, B8-x02); the old flowchart's vendor tracker is outdated.
Privacy: guest lists, budgets and family details only on the secure page. The AI never asks the budget (A4-50, B4-05). Texts to the couple, the owner and the planners carry only names, dates, times, places and the planner's fee (A6-15, B6-14, B8-01, B8-34, notes A8-45 and B8-44 on the page).
Licenses: none for planners in most places, so S1-60 and S1-63 take 'registration only' (2019-0451, 2020-1187) and S2-28 'No person license'; a seller-of-travel registration for a business that books guests' travel is a state-form switch in pf.license. Venue rules (load-in, end time, insurance certificates) are B4-34 and B4-70/B4-71 (Cedar Hill Farm needs a certificate naming it). The $2 applies: both companies pay it (the no-$2 branches are off).
Safety: the general danger check, plus the plug-in's: someone hurt or a fire at a venue stops a booking; thunder near an outdoor event gets 'everyone into a large building until 30 minutes after the last thunder' (B3-18, B8-30); a drunk guest or a fight goes to the venue's staff. The rain call on the day is own branch B8-x01; a late vendor is B8-x02.
Stand-ins: a wedding's date can't move. B7-56 keeps only 'A date that can't move' (B7-54: Carmen Ruiz with Gabe, or a full refund; no reply: nobody is swapped in and Sam calls; '2 New time' is off). In A, full planning stays with Nadia (A7-61 'Someone has it' off; A7-47 Sam calls).
Times: flow A keeps the master's Wed Oct 21 ask and Sat Oct 24, 11:00am visit (the first meeting); the call is Thu 12:00pm, the quote 1:00pm, signing 7:30 to 7:52pm, then Dec 5, 2026 and May 6, 2027 bills, the final receipt May 13, the rating Jun 14, 2027. Flow B: ask Mon Oct 19, call and quote Tue Oct 20, signed by 6:51pm, free-cancel reminder Fri Oct 23, the set day Apr 22, 2027, walkthrough Apr 17, rehearsal May 21, the day May 22 (DONE 12:20am), pay link and receipt Sun 9am, rating Mon May 24. Words ops set every step's time on the listed paths; sections 11 to 13 keep the master's business-day clock (Oct 22 to Nov 2), as other professions do.
Prices are the example's own, not a standard: full planning $8,500, partial $4,800, month-of $2,400, a planning consult or an extra meeting $150, an extra hour $150 a planner, a welcome party from $900, travel free to 40 miles then $1 a mile. Sam OKs quotes over $500 (B) and every planning quote (A).
Off (beyond the plug-in splits): walk-ins (the studio sees couples by booking), repeat plans, packages and gift cards, insurance and warranty plans, rushes, groups and seats, sent-now work, damage holds, crews, minimums, outside checks, permits, deliveries, items to the shop, rentals, aftercare, results later, free fixes, a 'problem that gets worse', late parts and tools, the 'nobody home' no-show at a wedding (B8-03), 'Missing: can't go ahead' (B8-45), the right-to-cancel refund for an extra hour given at once (B10-05), A8-23 (nothing of the couple's to note before a meeting) and the emergency higher-price branches (S12-20).
Renames: about 190 pairs in A and 125 in B; sentences first, then names, then trade words. Off ops name master labels; the build renames them the same way. Words ops for flow A use per-path variants (the full price, before and after key), and the master's less specific variants on those paths get the same words. keep: none.
hidden-words: 3 spots listed (A8-36 on the main path and the consult, A7-47 on the consult and the extra meeting); each reads right after the renames ('Your 1:30pm planning meeting will start about 1:45pm'; 'nobody else here does that service'), so none needed a change.
Not sure (for the reviewer): flow A's visit is the first planning meeting, with the later payments as bills after it; the extra planning meeting path (list|none|bill) dated two days after signing assumes a different, long-running contract; the free cancel in A ends 24 hours before the first meeting (the old flow said 3 days after signing); the example's cancel amounts; month-of coordination at $2,400 with a 25% retainer while full planning takes 30%; the rehearsal as a what-if branch; section 10 of flow A mixes after-the-meeting what-ifs with the after-the-wedding rating and final receipt.
Review (Oct 23): the installments read as due dates, each billed a week ahead (S1-42, S1-46, A6-14, plug-in). S11-56 in A no longer gives the consult a $75 deposit (partial planning 30% to 25%). No health or family detail in owner or staff texts (A8-38, B3-22). Section 10 of flow A starts back at meeting 1 (A10-05, A10-06). B7-37/B7-38: one more hour for both planners is $300. B4-30 40 miles; B4-28 every planning booking signs a contract; B8-69 no photographer example; B8-46 one button; B10-05 nothing waits; B4-71 the certificate is the business's own paper; B4-02 venue consults are the main company's; plug-in adds party coordination and a weather limit for Kim's backyard party.
Follow-up (Oct 23, coordinator's call): the venue consult is out of flow B. Consults are flow A only (studio or video, $150 paid in full). Flow B's plug-in lists a free first call instead; Kim, Tessa and Nora book free first calls (nothing taken), Lin misses a walkthrough (no money kept; Sam decides if it counts), Sam's own price is the extra hour ($200), and the price raise is the extra hour ($175 a planner from Nov 2). 
Money fix Oct 27 2026 (D65/D66): month-of coordination: the rest is charged to the saved card when the day is done; full planning: billed in stages, each when the planner texts DONE for it; party coordination: charged to the saved card when the party is done; corporate: on the bill after the event or the company's invoice. Any older wording above about a date or free-cancel moment for the rest is from the earlier pass and no longer applies.
